clue.text: System of numbering has its points

definitions.meaning: a playful second sense: a base-ten number may carry a dot separating whole from fraction

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the dot used in base-ten fractions, which is called by the answer's name plus 'point'.
explanation.definitionFit: The base-ten counting system is named for ten, and its numbers can carry a point before the fraction.

clue.text: Elderly lady wants to make bet

parts.note: to do is to make or perform
a wager is a bet

explanation.surface: An old woman wants to place a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A widow holding a title from her late husband, by extension any dignified old woman.

clue.text: Qualifying as lawyer, obliged to buy every, one a drink?

definitions.text: obliged to buy every, one a drink?
definitions.meaning: jokingly, summoned to the pub counter to pay for the round

explanation.walkthrough: A barrister in England is formally admitted to the bar of the court; the joke reads it as being summoned to a pub bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission as a barrister, read literally as being summoned to the pub counter.

clue.text: Sound month's puzzle

indicators.note: placed at the start, this word says that what follows is to be spoken

parts.note: May's, belonging to the fifth month

explanation.surface: A healthy puzzle set for this month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy but signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A labyrinth of paths is a puzzle to find the way through.

clue.text: Eagle in swooping descent

indicators.note: a bird swooping moves wildly, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An eagle dives down through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry or family line, as in descent from a noble house.

clue.text: Nothing to enjoy really

definitions.meaning: in tennis scoring, zero is called by this word

explanation.definitionFit: Tennis calls a zero score by the word for deep affection, and to adore something is to enjoy it greatly.

clue.text: Not much scope for such a company?

definitions.text: Not much scope for such a company?

parts.words: Not much scope for such a company?
parts.note: restricted range, and the term a British firm attaches to its name when shareholders' liability is capped

explanation.walkthrough: A British company's name may end with this word, meaning its owners' liability is capped.
explanation.definitionFit: Restricted in range, and the word marking a British company whose owners' liability is capped.

clue.text: Forbid to check round

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone forbids inspecting the circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal refusal to allow something, to block it.

clue.text: Opposed to keeping profit in a way

indicators.note: the word for profit is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
gain means profit

explanation.surface: Someone objects to holding on to earnings in a certain fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' just repeats the container idea that 'in' already signals; 'a way' is two pieces, the article plus the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile or contrary to, as in voting the other way.

clue.text: Be bold, valour doubly holding up

indicators.note: the two words for valour hold the next word between them

parts.note: valour is given twice, by two synonyms: pluck and courage
valour is given twice, by two synonyms: pluck and courage
taken as written

explanation.surface: Show daring: bravery twice over keeps you standing.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon nerve and act bravely, overcoming fear.

clue.text: Aussie dancing girl?

parts.note: read literally, a girl from Australia doing a ballroom turn in three-four time; really the famous Australian bush ballad

explanation.walkthrough: The song title, read word by word, is a girl's name with a ballroom dance verb in front of it, and the song is Australia's unofficial anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush ballad is Australia's best-known folk song, and its title reads as a girl doing a ballroom dance.

clue.text: Information about line of valley

indicators.note: the word for information is placed around the letter for line

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone gathers facts about the course of a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish word for a narrow valley, common in place names.

clue.text: A good man, we hold, is superfluous

indicators.note: the clue's word we is said to hold the other pieces, so it goes around them

parts.note: taken as written
ST, abbreviation for saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: A group claims that a certain virtuous man is unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste material or ground is surplus to requirements, left over and unwanted.

clue.text: Quickly look at medical procedure

definitions.meaning: to glance over a page quickly
an imaging examination of the body, such as by ultrasound

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to read rapidly and an imaging examination in hospital.

clue.text: Heathen had dish full of silver

indicators.note: the word for dish is filled with the symbol for silver

parts.note: a pan is a cooking dish
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A heathen owned a bowl brimming with silver coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of a non-mainstream or polytheistic religion, a non-believer.

clue.text: Tender proposal

definitions.meaning: to present formally, as one does a bid
a suggestion or bid put forward

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to present formally and a bid put forward.

clue.text: Living struggle of desert nation

parts.note: to rat is to desert one's side
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: The fight for survival among a people living in a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like the noun for arid land; here it is the verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitive scramble of working life is a struggle just to make a living.

clue.text: Failure to pay in notes a mistake

parts.note: D and E are two musical notes
a fault is an error

explanation.surface: Someone fails to pay a bill because of an error in the banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests banknotes, fitting the money surface, but gives two letter-named musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Not meeting a payment when due is the financial sense of the word.

clue.text: Yowl of disapproval

parts.note: a feline's yowl suggests a pet's cry, but the phrase means a jeering whistle from an audience

explanation.walkthrough: A yowl is literally a cat's call, and a jeer from a crowd is named that way.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill whistle or shout from a crowd expressing scorn, named after a feline's cry.

clue.text: Standard work found at Derby, for example

definitions.meaning: a book or piece of art of lasting recognised quality
the Derby is one of the five English horse races known by this name

explanation.walkthrough: The Derby, run at Epsom, is one of five big British flat races grouped under this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A definitive work of lasting value, and one of five major British horse races.

clue.text: Runs into thinner student

indicators.note: the letter for runs goes into the word for thinner

parts.note: leaner means thinner
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Jogging helps a slimmer pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone being taught, a pupil.

clue.text: One might bleat, being so swindled

definitions.text: One might bleat, being so swindled

parts.words: One might bleat, being so swindled
parts.note: a sheep, which bleats, has a woolly coat; to be so covered is also slang for being cheated

explanation.walkthrough: Something that bleats is a sheep, covered in wool; the word for having a woolly coat also means cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cheated of money, from shearing a sheep of its wool.

clue.text: Illness cast off, but still showing high temperature

parts.note: flu is an illness
to shed is to cast off

explanation.surface: Someone shook off an illness but still has a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Reddened in the face, as from fever or heat.

clue.text: In fact, graduates are of lower value

indicators.note: the graduates are put inside the word for fact

parts.note: a deed is a fact or action, as in 'in deed'
BAS, Bachelors of Arts, are graduates

explanation.surface: Graduates are actually worth less these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fact' looks like a phrase meaning actually; 'In' is the container signal and 'fact' gives DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Reduced in quality or worth, cheapened.

clue.text: Adam's son was competent, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word for competent is spoken, giving a name that sounds the same

parts.note: able means competent

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a son of Adam was capable.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the second son of Adam and Eve, killed by his brother Cain.

clue.text: Tricked at university and brought into court

parts.note: to be had is to be fooled
up means in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A student was deceived while at college and ended up facing a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom for being charged and made to appear before a magistrate.

clue.text: Not feeling miners get black

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' trade union
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Miners covered in coal dust lose all sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Without sensation, deadened, as a frozen hand is.

clue.text: Foreign character to live with army

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An alien goes to live with the military.
explanation.definitionFit: The second letter of the Greek alphabet, a letter from a foreign script.

clue.text: Fearful man, non-progressive at heart

indicators.note: the answer lies in the middle of the word given

explanation.surface: A frightening fellow, reactionary to the core.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating giant of fairy tales, a monster to be feared.

clue.text: Lurking danger not found in Irish meadows?

definitions.meaning: a hidden treacherous threat, a concealed enemy
legend has St Patrick driving all serpents out of Ireland, so no reptile lies in its fields

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the idiom literally: Ireland famously has no wild serpents.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a treacherous person or hidden peril, pictured literally as a serpent concealed in a meadow.

clue.text: Reasonable entertainment

definitions.meaning: a funfair with rides and stalls

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both just and an outdoor event with rides and stalls.

clue.text: Part of pool has profound purpose

parts.note: deep means profound
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Part of a swimming pool serves a serious function.
explanation.definitionFit: The section of a swimming pool where the water is too high to stand.
